commit_subject: Encode the whole-dollar rounding the FNS SNAP computation applies (#826)
description: Fixes #762 — the last residual class in the SNAP QC administrative-data oracle (TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-oracles#244): 33 of 856 Colorado FY 2024 replays differed by exactly $1 because the encoded chain carried cents where FNS computes in whole dollars.

evidence_check.normalization: casefold; whitespace runs collapsed to one space; number, date and code forms must not touch another digit

strings.text: Round down each income and allotment calculation that ends in 1 through 49 cents and round up each calculation that ends in 50 through 99 cents
Multiply the total gross monthly earned income by 20 percent and subtract that amount from the total gross income.
Subtract from total shelter costs 50 percent of the household's monthly income after all the above deductions have been subtracted. The remaining amount, if any, is the excess shelter cost.
Subtract the homeless shelter deduction, if any, up to the maximum of $143.

(ii) In calculating net monthly income, the State agency shall use one of the following two procedures: (A) Round down each income and allotment calculation that ends in 1 through 49 cents and round up each calculation that ends in 50 through 99 cents

nearest_quotes.quote: (ii) In calculating net monthly income, the State agency shall use one of the following two procedures:
(A) Round down each income and allotment calculation that ends in 1 through 49 cents and round up each calculation that ends in 50 through 99 cents; or

provision_review.why: These are the nearest passages, not decisive ones. 273.10(e)(1)(ii) lets the State agency choose between rounding to the nearest dollar under (A) and its TANF procedure under (B), and (B) allows keeping the cents. Carrying cents through the chain, as the pre-fix module does, is therefore allowed by the text. Picking (A) at the federal level, and the post-fix floor() that simply drops cents from the earned income deduction (which matches neither option), both rest on the FNS QC computation.
provision_review.missing_basis: The FNS SNAP quality-control technical documentation (FY2024, page 84) and the constructed FSERNDED/FSSLTDED/HOMELESS_DED values in the QC file. Those are what pick option (A), and drop-cents for the earned income deduction, out of the State-option election. Neither is in the bundle.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module carried cents through the entire net-income chain and so represented neither procedure of the 273.10(e)(1)(ii) rounding election the source says the State agency shall use — in particular the (e)(1)(ii)(A) round-down-1-to-49-cents / round-up-50-to-99-cents step on the excess shelter calculation — producing benefits a dollar off from the FNS computation.
triage.triage_notes: Single rule module in the commit (plus its companion test file and the encoding manifest). Read the cited provision through the pinned corpus release (us-sc-snap-2026-07-15, corpus commit 3932af44) and confirmed the source text verbatim: '(ii) In calculating net monthly income, the State agency shall use one of the following two procedures: (A) Round down each income and allotment calculation that ends in 1 through 49 cents and round up each calculation that ends in 50 through 99 cents; or (B) ...' — so the rounding clause is in the source and was absent from the pre-fix encoding. Three formulas changed inside this one module: snap_earned_income_deduction_for_net_income gained floor(...), and snap_homeless_shelter_deduction_for_net_income and snap_excess_shelter_cost gained floor(... + 0.5) (half-up nearest dollar). I picked snap_excess_shelter_cost for rule_path because it is the only one that also gained a new proof atom whose excerpt quotes the (e)(1)(ii)(A) election, making the source linkage decisive; the other two are equally part of the same defect. Caveat for a reviewer: the earned-income-deduction change is floor (drop cents), which is NOT literally the (e)(1)(ii)(A) half-up election — the commit and PR ground it empirically on the QC file's constructed FSERNDED values (earned 432 -> 86, 424 -> 84) and on the newly added checked_path us/guidance/usda/fns/snap-qc-fy2024-technical-documentation/page-84, i.e. on the computation FNS applies rather than on the (A) text alone. An alternative kind of amount_mismatch is defensible because the observable symptom was $1 benefit differences, but the fix adds a source-stated clause that was missing, so unrepresented_clause fits better. Non-fidelity changes ride along in the same diff and are mechanical: module rationale/summary prose, the source string on snap_earned_income_deduction_for_net_income ('7 CFR 273.10(e)(1)(i)(B) with the (e)(1)(ii) rounding election'), and the added checked_path. PR #826 has no reviews and no review or issue comments. The PR notes companion work #765 and a verification rerun landing on axiom-oracles#244, and states two pre-existing New York composition test failures are unrelated.
triage.verifier_justification: The pinned corpus release (us-sc-snap-2026-07-15) carries a mandatory rounding step inside the very paragraph the module encodes: "(ii) In calculating net monthly income, the State agency shall use one of the following two procedures: (A) Round down each income and allotment calculation that ends in 1 through 49 cents and round up each calculation that ends in 50 through 99 cents". The pre-fix module contained no rounding anywhere in the (e)(1) chain — grep of the parent blob shows rounding only at the (e)(2)(ii) 30-percent reduction and the minimum benefit — so the (e)(1)(ii) election was simply absent, and the fix adds it as a half-up step on the flagged rule plus a new proof atom at versions[0].formula bound to the verbatim (A) excerpt. This changes computed meaning, not presentation (33 of 856 Colorado replays moved by $1), which rules out mechanical, and it is a clause the source states rather than new coverage the module never claimed, which rules out not_a_defect. boundary_direction does not fit better because there was no rounding operator whose side was wrong, and amount_mismatch does not fit because no numeric value, rate, or threshold changed.
triage.verifier_notes: Two caveats a reviewer should see, neither of which overturns the verdict on the flagged rule_path. (1) The commit changes three formulas, and only two of them follow the (A) text. snap_earned_income_deduction_for_net_income becomes floor(...) (drop cents), which contradicts (A): the commit's own example, earned income 424 -> deduction 84, is 84.80, which (A) would round UP to 85. Its basis is the QC file's constructed FSERNDED ("empirically decisive over nearest-dollar"), i.e. agency practice, not the cited (A) election — closer to untraceable_branch/other if that sibling rule were the one being scored. The flagged rule (snap_excess_shelter_cost) is the well-grounded one: the commit says the regulation text "fixes the shelter direction the data alone cannot distinguish," and the added proof atom excerpt is verbatim (A). (2) Procedure (B) lets a State include cents in income calculations where its TANF program does, so a cents-carrying chain is not literally forbidden for every State; I considered this as grounds for not_a_defect and rejected it, because (B) itself ends "...and round the final shelter deduction amount," so the shelter deduction is rounded under either procedure, and because the module is a single national encoding with no State-election input for (e)(1)(ii). Worth noting the asymmetry: the module does parameterize the (e)(2)(ii) election via state_agency_rounds_thirty_percent_net_income_up but hardcodes (A) here.
